Consider the RCL circuit shown above. Given that the charge $q(t)$ of the capacitor at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
q(t)=A{e}^{-2t}+B{e}^{-t}+\frac{P}{10}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\frac{Q}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)
$$

where $A,$ $B,$ $P,$ and $Q$ are constants, find the value of $P+Q.$

*Hint: The voltage drop ${V}_{C}$ across the capacitor is related to its charge by $q=C{V}_{C},$ where $C$ is the capacitance measured in Farads.*
question.worked_solution:
The diagram shows a series RCL circuit with a source electromotive force (EMF) of $4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\,\text{V},$ a resistor of resistance $6\,Ω,$ a capacitor of capacitance $0.25\,\text{F},$ and an inductor of inductance $2\,\text{H}.$

The current $I,$ measured in amperes, is defined as the rate of flow of charge $q,$ measured in coulombs.

$$
I=\frac{dq}{dt}
$$

Kirchhoff's voltage law states that in a series circuit, the source voltage (EMF) equals the sum of the voltage drops.

In an RCL circuit, there are three voltage drops:

- The voltage drop across the resistor is proportional to the current, with a constant of proportionality $R=6\,Ω.$ So,

$$
{V}_{R}=6I=6\,\frac{dq}{dt}.
$$

- The voltage drop across the capacitor is related to its charge by $q=C{V}_{C}.$ Therefore,

$$
{V}_{C}=\frac{q}{C}=\frac{q}{0.25}=4q.
$$

- The voltage drop across the inductor is proportional to the rate of change of current, with a constant of proportionality $L=2\,\text{H}.$ Hence,

$$
{V}_{L}=2\,\frac{dI}{dt}=2\,\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dq}{dt})=2\,\frac{{d}^{2}q}{d{t}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, by Kirchhoff's voltage law, the differential equation governing the amount of charge $q$ on the capacitor is

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)=6\,\frac{dq}{dt}+4q+2\,\frac{{d}^{2}q}{d{t}^{2}},
$$

which gives

$$
\frac{{d}^{2}q}{d{t}^{2}}+3\cdot \frac{dq}{dt}+2q=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).
$$

The given equation is a second-order linear equation with constant coefficients. To find the general solution, we must sum the complementary and particular solutions.

- To find the complementary solution ${q}_{c},$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
\frac{{d}^{2}{q}_{c}}{d{t}^{2}}+3\cdot \frac{d{q}_{c}}{dt}+2{q}_{c}=0.
$$

Solving using an integration technique, such as a trial solution, we obtain the complementary solution

$$
{q}_{c}(t)=A{e}^{-2t}+B{e}^{-t},
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are constants.

- Next, we find the particular solution. Note that the right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is sinusoidal with argument $2t.$ So, we assume that the particular solution is also a sinusoidal with argument $2t,$ i.e.,

$$
{q}_{p}(t)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{p} & =\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t), \\ \frac{d{q}_{p}}{dt} & =-2\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+2\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t), \\ \frac{{d}^{2}{q}_{p}}{d{t}^{2}} & =-4\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-4\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\end{aligned}
$$

into the inhomogeneous equation and group like terms on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,(-4\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-4\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))+3(-2\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+2\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))\,\,\, &  \\ +2(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ (-2\alpha +6\beta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+(-6\alpha -2\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2\alpha +6\beta =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)) \\ -6\alpha -2\beta =2\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-\frac{3}{10},$ $\beta =-\frac{1}{10}.$ Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{q}_{p}(t)=-\frac{3}{10}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).
$$

Now, since the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary solution and the particular solution, the general solution in our case is

$$
q(t)={q}_{c}(t)+{q}_{p}(t)=A{e}^{-2t}+B{e}^{-t}-\frac{3}{10}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).
$$

Therefore, we have $P=-3,$ $Q=-1,$ and

$$
P+Q=-3+(-1)=-4.
$$
